articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
articles.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.

articles.title: State AGs fight Character AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats
articles.summary: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.

articles.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
articles.summary: ⁠Nvidia has made clear⁠ it won’t backstop an AI data center until it’s nearly ready to run, and that’s landing just as neoclouds report construction delays and more expensive debt. The message to developers is that land, power, and a finished building matter more than a pitch deck. ⁠Anita Verma-Lallian⁠ has been selling exactly that. […]

articles.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
articles.summary: Amazon and Meta are discussing a potential deal that would end a two-month-long blockade of Muse.

articles.title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
articles.summary: The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up and whether Huang's affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed's assurances.

articles.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
articles.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.

articles.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
articles.summary: As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.

articles.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
articles.summary: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.

articles.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
articles.summary: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.

articles.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
articles.summary: Anthropic’s post-IPO slump could put pressure on AI startup valuations.

articles.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
articles.summary: The British cyber agency says that "building strong foundations has never mattered more" as AI hacking tools rely on exploiting simple security flaws.

articles.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
articles.summary: The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent.

articles.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
articles.summary: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

articles.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
articles.summary: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power every year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.

articles.title: Pinterest will now let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see
articles.summary: While other social platforms have focused on restricting teens' access to AI chatbots, Pinterest is addressing the AI content filling their feeds.

articles.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
articles.summary: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart for a reported $7.5 billion is part of its efforts to improve the efficiency of its Trainium chips.

articles.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
articles.summary: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.

articles.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra
articles.summary: See how two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to find potential exoplanets in public data from NASA’s Kepler and TESS space telescopes.

articles.title: Clay helps sales teams win with Codex and ChatGPT
articles.summary: ChatGPT and Codex integrations help Clay’s users research deals and turn data into go-to-market plays, with GPT-6 models handling the reasoning.

articles.title: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
articles.summary: As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals.

articles.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
articles.summary: Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.

articles.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
articles.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux. It helps teams protect running systems while they roll out patches.

articles.title: Connected intelligence for in-house legal
articles.summary: Watch OpenAI’s Stacey Wang and Craig Bruney, Mary O’Carroll of LECG, and Cooley’s Richard Segal explore how AI can help in-house legal teams connect business context, build reusable workflows and get more from outside counsel.

articles.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
articles.summary: Richpanel uses GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT-6 Luna for their conversations.
